A triangular plate of mass $M$ occupies the region $D$ in the first quadrant enclosed by the line $y=1-x$ and the coordinate axes. The mass density at each point is proportional to the square of its distance from the $x$-axis. Find the moment of inertia of the plate about the $x$-axis.

activity_context.topic_title: Moments of Inertia of Laminas About the Coordinate Axes

feedback.problem:
A rectangular plate of mass $M$ occupies the region
$D={(x,y)\,:\,0\le x\le 3,\,\,0\le y\le 1}.$
The mass density at each point is proportional to its distance from the $x$-axis.
Find the moment of inertia of the lamina about the $y$-axis.
feedback.worked_solution:
For a plane lamina $D$ with mass density function $\lambda (x,y),$ we have the following definitions:

- The moment of inertia about the $x$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{x}={∬}_{D}{y}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is given by

$$
{I}_{y}={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

- The moment of inertia about the origin is given by

$$
{I}_{0}={∬}_{D}({x}^{2}+{y}^{2})\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A={I}_{x}+{I}_{y}.
$$

From the description, the mass density function can be written as

$$
\lambda (x,y)=k|y|=ky,
$$

where $k$ is a constant of proportionality. We can find an expression for $k$ in terms of $M$ by integrating the density function over the plate:

$$
\begin{aligned}M & ={∬}_{D}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}ky\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =k({\int }_{0}^{3}\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{1}y\,\text{d}y) \\  & =k[x]_{0}^{3}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =k(3-0)(\frac{1}{2}-0) \\  & =\frac{3k}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $k=\frac{2M}{3}$ and hence,

$$
\lambda (x,y)=ky=\frac{2M}{3}y.
$$

Therefore, the moment of inertia about the $y$-axis is

$$
\begin{aligned}{I}_{y} & ={∬}_{D}{x}^{2}\lambda (x,y)\,\text{d}A \\  & =\frac{2M}{3}{\int }_{0}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\cdot y\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}y \\  & =\frac{2M}{3}({\int }_{0}^{3}{x}^{2}\,\text{d}x)({\int }_{0}^{1}y\,\text{d}y) \\  & =\frac{2M}{3}\cdot {[\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3}]}_{0}^{3}\cdot {[\frac{1}{2}{y}^{2}]}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\frac{2M}{3}(9-0)(\frac{1}{2}-0) \\  & =3M.\end{aligned}
$$
